name: config_resource_delete

name.note: required for a named resourceType, empty for a singleton

preconditionToken.nativeLocation: the DELETE path itself: the signature is the route's last path parameter

targetId.collection: the default configuration collection only: the Target allowlist names a resource, so a caller-supplied collection is refused with invalid_argument
targetId.denialCodeSource: D30 §7, Tool-scoped; the Phase 3 machinery keeps operation_disabled

fixedKnobsNote: The documented DELETE route takes an optional `confirm` flag for a delete the Gateway says would affect other resources. The caller cannot choose it: it is never sent, so such a delete is refused like any other rejection and no call can authorize a cascade outside its Targets.

requestSchemaValidation.schema: not applicable: the documented DELETE route takes no request body, and nothing but the path is sent
requestSchemaValidation.appliesTo: the Target identity and the Resource signature, validated and percent-encoded before dispatch
requestSchemaValidation.unavailableDisposition: a documented delete route whose Target cannot be read back exposes no delete route, so the Tool refuses the resource type with unsupported_capability

rejectionPolicy.rule: D30 §2: an explicit Gateway rejection is the result of the attempt — a 4xx (including 409 for a stale signature, which D30 §7 maps to `conflict`) or a 2xx carrying success=false with a problem. No read-back may turn it into a success: a Target that is gone may have been deleted by another writer.
verificationMaySucceedWhen: the Gateway claimed success (2xx with no refusal)
rejectionPolicy.ambiguousAttribution: a competing writer cannot be ruled out for an ambiguous dispatch, so a read-back that shows the Target gone is outcome_unknown, never a success; the Target still holding the caller's signature is not_applied

verification: bounded re-read of the Target: the claimed success is confirmed only when no resource exists at it, and the absence is reported as the Observed state
